angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 372,200 km at 53.00 pc = 0.09 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 18.8696 +/- 0.0131 mas (same row, RUWE 1.16): 53.00 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.535 +/- 0.022 solar radii from Mistry et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-2068 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024PASA...41...30M/abstract): 372,200 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.559 +/- 0.027 solar masses from Mistry et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-2068 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024PASA...41...30M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3710 +/- 57 K from Mistry et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2068 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024PASA...41...30M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Mistry et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2068 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024PASA...41...30M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-2068.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.729, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
